title: Sanger Tree of Life HMW DNA Extraction: Manual Plant MagAttract v.5
author: Graeme Oatley

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a lysis buffer master mix in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (for n+1 samples) to the preheated lysis buffer immediately prior to initiating lysis, swirling the centrifuge tube to mix.
Place the lysis buffer on the 65 °C heat block and incubate at 400 rpm for at least 20 minutes; keep at temperature until added to the sample.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare cryogenically disrupted tissue samples for lysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the samples to a pre-chilled cold block on wet ice and incubate for 10 minutes to equilibrate temperature.
Transfer 50 mg of cryogenically disrupted tissue from each sample to 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Ensure tissue is completely disrupted into a fine powder; any samples with 'chunks' should be further cryogenically disrupted.

steps.title: Initial Lysis and RNase Treatment
steps.instruction: Perform initial lysis and remove RNA from the samples.

substeps.instruction: Add 370 µL of the preheated lysis buffer plus Proteinase K to each sample.
Immediately homogenise the lysate by mixing with 5 rapid pulse vortexes.
Place on the 55 °C heat block at 600 rpm for 15 minutes.
Add 4 µL RNase A to each sample and mix thoroughly by inversion until any aggregated, insoluble or sedimented tissue particles are resuspended.
Incubate for 5 minutes; resuspend any severely aggregated samples by pipette-mixing with a wide-bore pipette tip.

steps.title: Extended Lysis and Sedimentation
steps.instruction: Complete the lysis process and allow particles to settle.

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples for a further 45 minutes on the heat block at 55 °C at 600 rpm.
For the final 15 minutes of lysis, remove the 600 rpm mixing to allow aggregated, insoluble or sedimented tissue particles to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Remove sample tubes from the heat block and allow the lysate to settle to the bottom of the tube for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Lysate Recovery and Clarification
steps.instruction: Transfer the clarified lysate to new tubes and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Using a wide-bore pipette tip set to 380 µL, transfer each lysate to fresh individual microcentrifuge tubes, avoiding insoluble material.
Centrifuge the samples at 8000 rpm for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: DNA Binding to Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Bind the gDNA to Suspension G beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 280 µL Buffer MB to each sample and 40 µL of Suspension G beads.
Invert the tube 10 to 20 times to ensure beads are suspended in the lysate.
Allow 5 minutes for binding.
Spin down tubes in a mini centrifuge for 1–2 seconds.
Place tubes on the magnetic rack and allow 2–5 minutes for the beads to migrate (more viscous samples may take longer).
Remove the supernatant and discard.

steps.title: Bead Washing (MW1 and PE)
steps.instruction: Wash the bead-DNA complex using Buffer MW1 and Buffer PE.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µL Buffer MW1 directly to the bead pellet, invert 10 to 20 times to resuspend, place on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes, and discard supernatant. Repeat this wash for a total of two washes.
Add 700 µL Buffer PE directly to the bead pellet, invert 10 to 20 times to resuspend, place on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes, and discard supernatant. Repeat this wash for a total of two washes.
Briefly centrifuge the samples in a mini centrifuge to collect at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Nuclease-Free Water Wash
steps.instruction: Perform a final wash with nuclease-free water.

substeps.instruction: While tubes are on the magnetic rack, pipette 700 µL nuclease-free water onto the side opposite of the beads (do not pipette directly onto the pellet).
Incubate for exactly 1 minute, then slowly aspirate and discard water.
Briefly centrifuge the tubes in a mini centrifuge and place back on the magnetic rack.
Use a small micropipette to remove any residual wash buffer.

steps.title: gDNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the purified gDNA from the beads.

substeps.instruction: Remove samples from the magnetic rack and add 400 µL of Buffer AE directly to the bead pellet.
Mix by gently flick mixing or using a wide-bore pipette tip to dislodge the pellet.
Repeat this elution step for a total of two times.
Using a 200 μL wide-bore pipette tip, carefully transfer the supernatant containing purified gDNA to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.
Store the extracted gDNA sample at 4 ºC.

steps.title: 0.45X SPRI Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform a 0.45X SPRI cleanup manually or via KingFisher Apex.

substeps.instruction: Immediately add 180 μL of AMPure PB beads to 400 μL of DNA.
Vortex AMPure PB beads for 30 seconds.
Incubate the mix on the bench top for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Spin down tubes in a mini centrifuge for 1–2 seconds to collect the beads.
Mix the beads/DNA thoroughly by pipette-mixing 15 times with a wide-bore pipette tip (do not flick).
Place tubes in a magnetic bead rack and wait for the beads to pellet on the side of the tube (may take 5+ minutes).
Slowly dispense 80% ethanol (700–1000 µL for 1.5 mL tube) against the side of the tube opposite the beads without disturbing them.
Incubate samples overnight at room temperature.
Following overnight incubation, pipette-mix samples slowly 5 times with a wide-bore pipette tip.
Briefly centrifuge samples in a mini centrifuge and place on a magnetic rack for bead capture.

steps.title: Final Ethanol Washes and Elution
steps.instruction: Perform final washes and recover the purified DNA.

substeps.instruction: Wash beads with freshly prepared 80% ethanol. Spin down for 1-2 seconds, return to magnetic rack to pellet, and aspirate/dispose of remaining ethanol. Repeat for a total of two ethanol washes.
Set the heat block to 37 °C and label two sets of 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes for each sample.
Slowly pipette off cleared supernatant and save in the first labelled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the beads.
Briefly spin down tubes for 1–2 seconds and place on the magnetic rack to allow beads to pellet (up to 5+ minutes).
Incubate tubes on the heat block at 37 °C for 30 minutes at 350 rpm.
Remove tubes from the magnetic rack and add 135 µL of EB buffer to the beads.
Gently mix by slowly pipetting 15 times with a wide bore pipette tip (do not flick).
Slowly pipette off cleared supernatant and save in the second labelled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the beads.
Proceed samples directly to QC; if successful, the first set of supernatants can be discarded.
